title: Micro Run Notebook - Aditya
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal ledger for tiny micro-bench runs — velocity over polish. Use for ad-hoc changes (quant, batching, small seq len) and capture quick comparisons before moving into the official bench harness.

Table (CSV-style paste-friendly):
run_id, date, model, quant, batch_size, seq_len, tokens_out, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cost_per_k_tokens_usd, notes
MR-001, 2026-02-20, vicuna-13b, fp16, 1, 64, 128, 42, 91, 0.85, baseline fresh container, no cache
MR-002, 2026-02-20, vicuna-13b, int8, 1, 64, 128, 38, 83, 0.62, int8 quant w/ distillation knobs
MR-003, 2026-02-21, vicuna-13b, int8, 4, 64, 512, 58, 120, 0.18, batching 4 improved unit cost but p95 up
MR-004, 2026-02-22, lla-mini-8b, fp16, 1, 128, 256, 28, 65, 0.45, small model quick win for short prompts
MR-005, 2026-02-25, vicuna-13b, int8-qk, 1, 64, 128, 35, 76, 0.55, trying qk-aware quant (cache compatibility?)
MR-006, 2026-03-01, vicuna-13b, int8, 1, 512, 1024, 140, 310, 1.1, long seq stress; kernel fallback observed at ~800
MR-007, 2026-03-03, vicuna-13b, int8, 8, 64, 1024, 85, 220, 0.12, heavy batching with async queue, trace id T-1223
MR-008, 2026-03-05, vicuna-13b, int8, 1, 64, 128, 36, 78, 0.60, repro of MR-002 on different host, slightly higher p95
MR-009, 2026-03-08, lla-mini-8b, int4, 1, 128, 256, 22, 50, 0.20, int4 prototype, need accuracy check vs eval set
MR-010, 2026-03-10, vicuna-13b, int8, 2, 128, 256, 62, 140, 0.30, dual-stream batching + KV cache warm

Quick takeaways / notes-to-self:
- int8 consistently reduces cost ~25-40% vs fp16 for short runs; watch p95 (regressions often show there).
- batching >4 gives good token-level cost but increases p95 unless async queueing is tuned. MR-007 looked promising but introduces head-of-line delays for small requests.
- KV cache warm dramatically drops p50 but first token/time-to-first-byte depends on kernel path. See MR-006 kernel fallback at seq ~800 — follow up with infra team.
- int4 shows promising cost number (MR-009) but need to validate hallucination/accuracy against eval set before recommending.

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Add small pinned eval (5 prompts) to each run row for quick quality signal (accuracy/eta).
- [ ] Re-run MR-003 with p50/p95 histograms exported (change bench harness flag).
- [ ] Create GH branch with small batching async prototype (linked PR GH:infra/serve#452) and link back here.
- [ ] Ask SRE if kernel fallback logs can be surfaced to user-level traces (ticket JIRA-PLT-987).

Open questions:
- How to capture cold-start TTFB separately from per-token p50? (currently conflating in p50 column)
- Is there a cheap way to log per-request batch size distribution for async queueing?

Handy commands / notes:
- local runner: ./bench/run_local.sh --model vicuna-13b --quant int8 --bs 1 --seq 64 --out csv
- quick diff: awk -F, '{print $1","$8","$9}' runs.csv | column -s, -t

References / pointers:
- Slack thread: #runtime-bench "int8 batching experiment" (ts 1678234)
- GH prototype: GH:infra/serve#452 (async-batch-queue)
- Confluence (team guide): confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLT/bench-harness (copy-paste note)

Scratch log (short):
- 2026-02-20 morning: MR-001 baseline to set numbers. small drift vs last month (~+3ms p50).
- 2026-02-25: tried qk-aware quant; saw ~5% latency improvement but uncertain memory tradeoff.
- 2026-03-01: long seq test exposed kernel fallback, capture attached trace id T-1134 in GH.

If I forget: re-run MR-003 + export p95 hist and attach to ticket JIRA-PLT-987.

-- adi
